body.objective: Students will be able to name foods and drinks.
body.iCan: I can name foods and drinks.
successCriteria: I can name common foods and drinks in Mandarin
I can say what I like to eat and drink with 喜欢 and 不喜欢
I can describe regional Chinese foods
body.hook: Dumplings, noodles, rice, tea: Chinese food is enjoyed worldwide, and it varies hugely by region, from spicy Sichuan dishes to Cantonese dim sum. Food words are some of the most useful you'll learn.

study.title: 好吃!
study.question: What foods and drinks can I name in Mandarin?
study.passage:
Food words (written for this lesson): 米饭 rice, 面条 noodles, 饺子 dumplings, 包子 steamed buns, 鸡肉 jīròu chicken, 牛肉 niúròu beef, 鱼 yú fish, 菜 cài vegetables / dish, 水果 shuǐguǒ fruit, 苹果 píngguǒ apple; drinks: 茶 tea, 水 water, 牛奶 niúnǎi milk, 果汁 guǒzhī juice.
Verbs: 吃 chī (eat), 喝 hē (drink).
Likes: 我喜欢吃饺子。我不喜欢喝牛奶。你喜欢吃什么?
好吃 hǎochī = delicious (food); 好喝 hǎohē = tasty (drink).
Regional food (general): northern China: wheat foods like noodles, dumplings and steamed buns; southern China: rice is the main staple; Sichuan: spicy food with Sichuan pepper; Guangdong (Cantonese): dim sum.
Culture: chopsticks (筷子 kuàizi) shouldn't be stuck upright in a rice bowl, because that resembles incense at funerals.
Activity: picture sort into 吃 and 喝, then a class survey: 你喜欢吃什么? 你喜欢喝什么?
study.source: Original activity written for this lesson; regional food notes are general.
steps: Say likes with 喜欢 and 不喜欢
discussion: Why are there two verbs, 吃 and 喝?
How is northern food different from southern food?
Why shouldn't chopsticks stand in rice?
What does the class like most?
study.product: Write eight sentences about food and drinks you like and don't like, and two sentences about regional Chinese food.

body.objective: Students will be able to use 想要 and measure words.
body.iCan: I can use 想要 and measure words.
successCriteria: I can use 想要 and 要 to say what I want
I can use food measure words 杯, 碗, 盘 and 个
body.hook: You can't say "a tea" or "two noodles" in Mandarin. You need a measure word: 一杯茶 (a cup of tea), 两碗面 (two bowls of noodles). With 想要, you can politely ask for exactly what you want.

study.title: 我想要…
study.question: How do I ask for food with measure words?
study.passage:
Grammar (written for this lesson):
Number + measure word + noun: 一杯茶 (a cup of tea), 两杯水 (two glasses of water), 一碗米饭 (a bowl of rice), 一碗面条 (a bowl of noodles), 一盘饺子 (a plate of dumplings), 一瓶果汁 (a bottle of juice), 一个包子 (a steamed bun).
Wanting: 我想要一杯茶。(I'd like a cup of tea; softer.) 我要一碗面条。(I want a bowl of noodles; direct but normal when ordering.)
Adding: 我还要一瓶水。(I also want a bottle of water.)
Questions: 你想要什么? (What would you like?) 你要几碗? (How many bowls?)
请 qǐng at the start makes requests polite: 请给我一杯水。(Please give me a glass of water.)
Activity: "Measure word match": match food pictures to measure words, then partners order from a picture menu: 我想要两盘饺子和一杯茶。
study.source: Original activity written for this lesson.
discussion: Why does Mandarin need measure words with food?
How is 想要 different from 要?
Which measure word goes with rice?
study.product: Write eight food requests using four different measure words, 想要, 还要 and 请.

body.objective: Students will be able to order at a restaurant.
body.iCan: I can order at a restaurant.
successCriteria: I can order food at a restaurant in Mandarin
I can ask for the bill and respond to the server
I can describe restaurant customs in Chinese culture
body.hook: In many Chinese restaurants, dishes are shared at a round table with a lazy Susan, and the host often orders for everyone. Today you'll order a meal in Mandarin and learn some table manners.

vocabulary.term: 还要别的吗? hái yào bié de ma
好吃极了 hǎochī jí le

study.title: 在饭馆
study.question: How do I order a meal in a Chinese restaurant?
study.passage:
Dialogue (read in threes):
服务员: 你们好! 这是菜单。你们想吃什么?
小李: 我们要一盘饺子、一碗牛肉面和一盘炒菜。
服务员: 喝什么?
小王: 两杯茶, 谢谢。
服务员: 还要别的吗?
小李: 就这些。
(later) 小王: 服务员, 买单!
服务员: 一共八十五块。
Pinyin highlights: Nǐmen xiǎng chī shénme? / Hái yào bié de ma? / Jiù zhèxiē. / Fúwùyuán, mǎidān! / Yígòng bāshíwǔ kuài.
Menu (prices in 块 kuài, yuan): 饺子 (一盘) 25; 牛肉面 (一碗) 30; 炒菜 (一盘) 20; 米饭 (一碗) 3; 茶 (一杯) 5; 果汁 (一杯) 10.
Customs: dishes are usually shared; it's polite to serve others before yourself; hosts often insist on paying; tapping two fingers on the table can be a quiet thank-you when someone pours your tea (common in southern China).
Activity: groups role-play ordering for three people from the menu and the server calculates the total.
study.source: Original dialogue and menu written for this lesson.
steps: Use the menu and measure words
discussion: How does the server ask "Anything else?"
How do you ask for the bill?
What is the total of the dialogue's order?
How is sharing dishes different from Canadian restaurants?
study.product: Role-play ordering a meal for three in Mandarin, with at least five dishes or drinks, asking for the bill and stating the total.
